issues.t: "Service High Voltage System" warning with reduced power
issues.sym: A "Service High Voltage System" or "Service Vehicle Soon" message appears, often with "Reduced Acceleration, Drive With Care." The car may refuse to charge, lose cabin heat, or the 12-volt battery may go flat. It often shows up while charging or right after a software update.
issues.why: Honda traced many of these warnings to a calibration problem in the battery energy control module, the computer that manages the high-voltage battery. Service Bulletin 25-043 covers every 2024-2025 Prologue.
issues.next: If power is reduced, drive gently to a safe place and contact a Honda dealer. Ask for the battery control module software update and resets in Service Bulletin 25-043. If the warning comes back after the update, insist on deeper diagnosis under the EV warranty.

issues.t: Clicking or popping from the front axles when turning
issues.sym: A clicking, ratcheting, clunking or popping noise from the front of the car during tight or low-speed turns, and sometimes when pulling away. It can start before 1,000 miles and often gets louder over time.
issues.why: The front drive axles and their CV joints are the usual source. Hundreds of owners have reported it. A December 2025 Honda tech line article quoted by owners tells dealers to inspect the axles and replace them only if damage is found, and some replaced axles have made the same noise again.
issues.next: Have a Honda dealer inspect the front axles and write the complaint on the repair order even if no damage is found, so it is documented under warranty. If you feel vibration, hear grinding, or lose drive power, stop driving and have the car towed.

issues.t: High-voltage battery pack fails at low mileage
issues.sym: Charging stops partway or will not start, with "high voltage battery" and "service vehicle soon" messages. Some cars were reported this way at only 500 to 1,000 miles.
issues.why: Dealers found failed modules inside the high-voltage battery pack, or an internal short, on some early cars. The fix was a new or repaired pack, and parts were often backordered for weeks.
issues.next: Do not keep trying to charge a car that shows a battery failure message. Contact a Honda dealer; the drive battery is covered by Honda's EV component warranty. Ask about a loaner or rental if parts are delayed.

issues.t: Heater blows cold or stops working
issues.sym: The heater blows cold air, sometimes on the highway in freezing weather, and the windshield can fog up. It may come on together with a high-voltage system warning.
issues.why: The Prologue heats the cabin with the same coolant system that warms and cools the drive battery. Owners report failed valves or other parts in that system, and the battery control software can also shut heat off when it sees a fault.
issues.next: If the windshield fogs, pull over safely and use the defrost or open a window until it clears. Have the dealer check the heating and battery thermal system and ask about software updates.

issues.t: Dead 12-volt battery, car won't power on
issues.sym: The car will not turn on or shift out of park even though the big drive battery is charged. Screens may stay dark, and doors may not unlock normally.
issues.why: Like gas cars, the Prologue uses a small 12-volt battery to wake up its computers. Software faults and high-voltage system errors can drain it, and Honda's high-voltage bulletin includes charging and testing the 12-volt battery as a step.
issues.next: Jump-start or charge the 12-volt battery following the owner's manual, then have the dealer test it and check for software updates. Replace it if it fails a load test.

issues.t: Gauge cluster and center screen can go blank (recall)
issues.sym: The instrument cluster and center touchscreen go black while driving, hiding your speed and warning lights. The backup camera image may not show in reverse. It can come and go and may clear after a restart.
issues.why: A software error in the radio control module can stop it from displaying information. Recall 26V-112 covers about 45,500 Prologues built from October 2023 to December 2024.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Check your VIN for open recalls. A Honda dealer will update the radio control module software for free; this update is not done over the air.

issues.t: Backup camera image blank or distorted (recall)
issues.sym: When you shift into reverse, the rearview camera picture is blank, scrambled or distorted.
issues.why: Some rearview cameras are faulty. Honda estimates only about 5% of the cars in recall 26V-306 have the defect but is replacing the camera on all of them as a precaution.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Until the free camera replacement is done, use your mirrors and look over your shoulder when backing up.

issues.t: Right front lower control arm may crack (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning before it breaks. A cracked arm could cause clunking, wandering steering, or a sudden loss of control.
issues.why: A manufacturing defect in the right front lower control arm can let it fracture. Recall 24V-540 covers a small number of early 2024 Prologues.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A Honda dealer will inspect the arm and replace it for free if needed.

issues.t: Sudden automatic braking with nothing in the way
issues.sym: The car brakes hard on its own while driving or backing up, or shows collision warnings when nothing is there. Some owners report it with adaptive cruise control on.
issues.why: Owners report false triggers from the automatic emergency braking and rear cross-traffic braking systems, which rely on cameras and radar sensors. No recall covers it.
issues.next: Keep sensors and the windshield camera area clean. Report each event to the dealer and to NHTSA. Ask the dealer to check sensor aim and software; some systems can be turned down or off in settings while you wait for a fix.

issues.t: Car won't charge or charge port damaged
issues.sym: Charging will not start or keeps stopping, a charge port door alert stays on, or the charging inlet shows burn marks.
issues.why: Owners report faults in the charging inlet and charge port door, and charging can also be blocked by high-voltage system errors.
issues.next: Stop using a charge port that looks burned or melted. Try another charger to rule out the station, then have a Honda dealer inspect the inlet and check for software updates.

issues.t: Car shifts to neutral while driving
issues.sym: While driving in Drive, the car suddenly shifts itself to neutral and stops pulling.
issues.why: The Prologue uses electronic shifting with no mechanical link, so a software or sensor fault can drop it into neutral. Owners have reported this on 2024 models.
issues.next: Steer to a safe stop with your hazards on. Try shifting back to Drive. Report it to the dealer right away and ask them to save any stored codes.

issues.sym: The blind spot warning lights in the mirrors don't come on when cars are beside you, or the system shows as unavailable.
issues.why: The rear corner radar sensors or their software can fault. Dirt, ice or a bumped bumper can also block them.
issues.next: Clean the rear bumper corners. If the warning stays off, have a dealer check the sensors. Always check your mirrors and look over your shoulder.

issues.sym: Wireless CarPlay disconnects during drives, and audio or navigation cuts out.
issues.why: Owners and reviewers report connection dropouts in the infotainment system's wireless phone projection.
issues.next: Keep your phone and the car's software up to date. A USB cable connection is often more stable. Report it to the dealer so they can check for updates.
